Clca 22 to 31 inches. light brownish gray (10YR 6/2) light clay loam, dark grayish brown (10YR 4/2) moist; massive; hard, friable, slightly sticky and plastic; strongly effervescent; common, fine soft masses of segregated lime; clear wavy boundary.
C2 31 to 60 inches, light gray (10YR 7/2) fine sandy loam, brown (10YR 5/3) moist; massive; slightly hard, friable, nonsticky and slightly plastic; strongly effervescent; a few fine, soft masses of lime.
The noncalcareous part of the soil ranges from 10 to 15 inches. The dark surface layer is 8 to 12 inches thick. Color hue is 10YR through 2.5Y. A horizon thickness ranges from 3 to 5 inches. Texture is loam, silt loam, or very fine sandy loam. Color range is grayish brown and dark grayish brown. The B2t horizon texture is heavy loam or clay loam with clay range of 25 to 35 percent and 15 to 35 percent sand coarser than very fine. The Bca and Cca horizons have color range of the pale brown, light brownish gray, and light gray. Lime is segregated in few to common fine and medium soft masses and threads.
Wages soils occur with Nunn, McRae, and Haverson soils. They have a less clayey B2t horizon than the Nunn soils. They have a B2t horizon not present in the McRae and Haverson soils.
Wages loam, 2 to 4 percent slopes (Wb)
This soil is on terraces and fans in river valleys and their major tributaries. Areas range in size from 5 to 30 acres. The soil has a profile similar to the typical one described for the series. In the valleys draining burned shale highlands, there are porcelanite gravels on the surface and in the soil. These areas include profiles with reddish brown color.
The surface runoff is slow and the erosion hazard is slight.
This soil is suited to irrigated and dryland crops. It is also suited to range.
(Capability Unit IIIe-3 Dryland; IIe-1 Irrigated; Sity range site 10-14 inch precipitation zone; Windbreak Suitability Group 1).
Wages loam, 4 to 3 percent slopes (Wc)
This soil is on fans on footslopes in intermittent stream valleys. The areas range in size from 10 to 20 acres. The soil has the profile described as typical for the series. Reddish brown color and procelanite gravel occur in the profiles of the burned shale highlands.
The surface runoff is medium, and the erosion hazard is moderate.
